title: Republic of Kenya
capsule: Kenya achieved independence from Britain on 12 December 1963 under Prime Minister Jomo Kenyatta, becoming a republic in December 1964; Kenyatta governed until his death in 1978, when Daniel arap Moi succeeded him and ruled under a formal one-party system (KANU) until international pressure forced multiparty constitutional amendments in 1991. Mwai Kibaki's election in December 2002 marked the first peaceful transfer of power to an opposition candidate, but disputed elections in December 2007 triggered ethnic violence killing over 1,100 people before a power-sharing accord brokered by Kofi Annan stabilized the government in 2008. Kenya is the largest economy in East Africa, driven by tea, horticulture, tourism, remittances, and a growing technology sector centered in Nairobi.
